experiment_template.research_question: Does the fixed successful GLM repair workflow transfer to three unused Svelte tasks, and how do 12K and 32K natural-history windows compare?
stop_conditions: 24 model calls and48 tokenizer calls per episode; zero retries.
Infrastructure failure pauses the fixed comparison; never replace model failure.

success_criteria.accounting: Admission, retained reasoning, projection, budgets and cleanup audited.
success_criteria.correctness: Submitted patches scored against all task-specific labels; every passing candidate reproduced.
success_criteria.coverage: All six preregistered cells retained, including no-patch and infrastructure outcomes.
success_criteria.isolation: Same paired initial prompts; no private model inputs or mid-matrix tuning.

records.falsifier: No transfer, accounting violations, or no observed improvement in the paired larger-window cells.
records.mechanism: Vary only context limits while holding selected tasks, public evidence, model, tools and budgets fixed; retain all outcomes.
records.scope: Three within-repository task pairs, one sample per cell; descriptive evidence only.
records.statement: The fixed workflow can repair previously unused same-repository tasks; a larger context window may reduce recovery overhead or improve correctness.

records.falsifier: Paired larger-window runs recover facts lost by smaller-window runs and uniquely pass full evaluation, with trace evidence connecting the retained fact to the correct repair.
records.mechanism: If source facts remain available but the proposed mechanism is wrong, retaining more history changes cost and recovery frequency without repairing the reasoning error.
records.scope: Three within-repository pairs; observations suggest hypotheses but cannot establish a causal window effect.
records.statement: Larger context alone does not improve repair correctness because the limiting factor is causal diagnosis or exact edit construction within the fixed call budget.
